title: Software
Software
text:
raterevision
Reproducible workflows for revising insurance rate tables
raterevision is an R package built around the idea that a rate revision should preserve a clear chain from current rates to proposed rates.
It provides tools for working with rate tables outside the rating engine itself: exporting tables for review or editing, importing them back into R, applying programmatic changes, and evaluating the effect of those changes using ratingtables.
A revision can therefore be expressed as a readable sequence of changes rather than only as a final collection of replacement tables.

Typical workflow

Start with the current rating tables.
Export selected tables to Excel when manual review or editing is useful.
Apply rate changes either programmatically or through an import workflow.
Use ratingtables to rate current and proposed plans.
Measure overall and segment-level effects.
Preserve the code and resulting tables as a reproducible record of the revision.

raterevision is currently available from GitHub and is not yet on CRAN.
install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("gs-actuary/raterevision")

aglmtools
Development-stage tools for interpretable regularized GLMs
aglmtools is an R project exploring actuarial applications of regularized generalized linear models with interpretable feature transformations.
The project includes cumulative ordered encodings inspired by Accurate GLM approaches, elastic-net estimation, and tools for handling common actuarial predictor structures such as ordered numeric variables and categorical effects.
This project is less mature than ratingtables, actuarialfitdist, and raterevision; the GitHub repository is the best place to follow its current development.

title: About
text:
I am a property and casualty actuary and data scientist with experience in insurance pricing, predictive modeling, ratemaking, and model governance.
Much of my technical work has focused on generalized linear models and other predictive methods, translating model results into practical rating structures, and building workflows that make actuarial analysis easier to explain, validate, reproduce, and implement.
I work primarily in R and have also worked with a broader modeling and production stack including gradient boosting, regularized regression, APIs, and related data-science tooling.

title: About
text:
Sollenberger Actuarial Technologies
Sollenberger Actuarial Technologies is a vehicle for publishing open-source actuarial software, demonstrations, and related technical work.
The projects are motivated by problems that arise repeatedly in actuarial practice: rating systems that are difficult to audit, rate revisions that lose their history in spreadsheets, models that are hard to translate into implementation, and analytical workflows that are difficult for someone else to reproduce.
The aim is not to replace actuarial judgment with software. It is to make the technical machinery around that judgment clearer and easier to work with.

title: About
text:
Open-source work
Current projects include:

ratingtables, a table-driven insurance rating engine;
raterevision, tools for reproducible rate-table revision workflows; and
aglmtools, a development-stage project for interpretable regularized GLMs.

I am particularly interested in feedback from people trying to use these tools on real rating structures and implementation workflows. Practical edge cases are often the most useful source of ideas for improving the software.

section: Actuarial technology, built in the open
text:
Actuarial technology, built in the open
The projects published here grow out of recurring actuarial problems: representing complex rating plans clearly, preserving an auditable chain from current to proposed rates, fitting useful predictive models, and making analytical work easier to validate and implement.
The emphasis is on tools that are:


Transparent
Calculations and model structures should be inspectable rather than hidden behind opaque interfaces.


Reproducible
Important analytical and rating decisions should be expressible in code, version controlled, and repeatable.


Practical
Software should fit real actuarial workflows, including Excel interaction, implementation review, auditing, and production use.

title: Sollenberger Actuarial Technologies, LLC
text:
Current projects


ratingtables
A lightweight, table-driven R rating engine for executing insurance rating plans from normalized factor tables and an ordered calculation specification.
It supports coverage-specific specifications, entity-level rating and aggregation, rate-set selection, validation, and optional step-by-step calculation traces.
Learn more · GitHub · CRAN


raterevision
An R package for managing rate-table revisions around a table-driven rating workflow.
It supports exporting and importing rate tables through Excel as well as programmatic rate changes that preserve a clear record of how proposed rates were produced.
Learn more · GitHub · Demos


aglmtools
A development-stage R project for interpretable regularized generalized linear modeling, including cumulative ordered encodings and actuarial-oriented handling of numeric and categorical predictors.
Learn more · GitHub
